title: A KINDNESS THAT OPENED A DOOR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the girls returned to Reuel their father, he asked them, "Why have you returned so early today?" They answered, "An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds. He even drew water for us and watered the flock." "And where is he?" Reuel asked his daughters. "Why did you leave him? Invite him to have something to eat."" - Exodus 2:18-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The daughters go home early for once, and their father wants to know why. Their answer is full of gratitude — he rescued us, he even drew the water for us. Notice they call him an Egyptian. To them he looked like the very nation that was enslaving his own people. Moses did not belong anywhere.

Then comes Reuel's response, which is beautifully simple: where is he? Why did you leave him? Invite him to eat.

This is hospitality in its purest form. A stranger with no known background, no references, no story — and the instinct is to bring him to the table.

The New Testament keeps pressing this on us. Practise hospitality. Do not neglect to show it to strangers (Heb 13:2). In our busy, guarded lives, the open table has quietly disappeared. Yet it remains one of the simplest ways to show the love of Christ.

Moses' entire next chapter of life began with a shared meal.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did I last open my home to someone outside my circle?
2. Am I grateful enough to speak well of those who have helped me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me an open home and an open heart. Help me to welcome the stranger the way You have welcomed me. Amen.
